turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you doing right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A bit tired today, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My nephew's visiting for a week and I need a game we can both enjoy. He's eleven.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, a handful of options. Listen first, I'll say when I'm finished.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a co-op platformer where we each play a little robot and help each other across levels.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's also obsessed with a football game, though I'm terrible at it and he'd crush me.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or a monster catching adventure on the handheld, which we could each play and then trade.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The robot platformer is built for exactly this, two people helping each other, so nobody feels left out. The football game might be fun for him but frustrating for you. The monster game works if you like doing your own thing side by side.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nora, can you check if the dishwasher actually ran?

turns.speaker: other
turns.text: It did, the plates are hot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've always wanted to make my own little game. I can't code at all. Moshi, is that hopeless?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not hopeless at all. There are free game engines with visual scripting, where you connect blocks instead of writing code.
